prediction_ref.short_label: Inference-ASIC cohort gains a fourth named buyer-designed chip by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: OpenAI-Broadcom Jalapeno unveil (June 24) is the precipitating origin signal for this thesis. OpenAI and Broadcom debuted Jalapeno, OpenAI's first custom inference accelerator and the first chip from a multi-year co-design effort, framed as an 'Intelligence Processor' architected around LLM inference rather than training. Engineering samples are already running machine-learning workloads in the lab at production target frequency and power, OpenAI claims performance per watt 'substantially better than current state-of-the-art,' and initial data-center deployment is targeted by end of 2026 at gigawatt scale. The platform is rack-scale: Broadcom's Tomahawk fabric (up to 1.6 terabits per second) wires the accelerators together and Celestia is co-designing the server rack. The structural read in today's reporting is exactly the prediction's premise -- the largest frontier-model buyer is now following the hyperscaler playbook of designing its own inference ASIC to escape merchant-GPU economics, placing a named OpenAI-Broadcom part alongside the Google-Broadcom TPU and Amazon Trainium lineage. The gap to the falsifiable bar: the cohort's fourth member is not yet here. No additional frontier-model buyer (Anthropic, Meta, xAI, or Microsoft) has publicly committed to or unveiled its own rack-scale inference accelerator, and the falsifiable core requires a named part or firm public commitment -- not a 'exploring custom silicon' rumor, and not an extension of an existing TPU or Trainium line.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agentic coding platforms ship token budgets and caps as default by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Gartner agentic-coding token-economics note (June 24) is the origin signal and reads as the product spec for this thesis. Gartner predicts that by 2028 the cost of AI coding will surpass the average developer's salary, driven by rising LLM token consumption and the shift to consumption-based pricing for agentic coding tools. The quotable thresholds are the news: 23 percent of technology leaders already spend $200-$500 per developer per month on tokens, and 6 percent of organizations pay more than $2,000 per developer per month. Gartner pins the steepest cost escalation on ungoverned autonomy in agent-driven workflows, bloated context windows, and the absence of structured feedback to optimize usage, naming the autonomous-developer-loop tools (the Cursor / Claude Code / Codex CLI class of agentic IDEs) as the per-seat cost center, and reframes the productivity narrative as a governance problem requiring a governed engineering operating model before scaled agent deployment outruns the gains. That diagnosis is the spec for the predicted default feature set: per-seat and per-team token budgets, hard and soft caps, real-time usage dashboards, and policy guardrails on autonomy depth and context-window size. The gap to the bar: this is an analyst projection, not a shipped product. No major agentic-coding platform has yet shipped admin-side consumption-governance controls as on-by-default features; the prediction needs vendors to make the spend-governance layer table stakes by Q2 2027.
